title: Cross-corpus portability with open-ended evaluation and a head-to-head against intermediate-step supervision
description: Move the evaluation off synthetic disease-specific multiple-choice items: construct the context-graph supervision on a text-attributed corpus with triple-to-passage provenance (e.g., an extraction pipeline over an open corpus, or a KG-text alignment resource such as CDTP), ask open-ended multi-hop questions, and score with exact match/F1 per hop depth. Include a head-to-head comparison against the strongest alternative answer to the same missing-supervision problem - learned intermediate-step supervision (teacher-student intermediate entity distributions) - at matched budget.
why_differs: The closest work validates only on two GraphMERT-extracted disease-specific KGs with synthetically generated multiple-choice items; this modification changes corpus, question format, and metric, and pits context-triple supervision against the alternative supervision-enrichment mechanism from the literature rather than only against its own KG-only baseline.
technical_mechanism: Retain the passage identifier for every extracted triple so that context graphs can be rebuilt for any hop path; generate multi-hop questions whose supporting path spans at least three hops; train the same backbone under the supervision arms; evaluate with per-hop exact match and F1, plus a hop-depth breakdown to test whether any context advantage grows with depth outside the MCQ setting.
expected_benefit: Tests whether the mechanism is domain-general and metric-robust rather than an artifact of generated domain MCQs, and separates two competing remedies for missing multi-hop supervision (added factual context versus added intermediate reasoning supervision).
potential_novelty: Moderate and hedged: context-triple supervision has not been evaluated on standard or open-ended benchmarks in the retrieved literature (G002), but the contribution is transfer evidence rather than a new mechanism.
implementation_difficulty_basis: Needs corpus selection, KG extraction with provenance retention, open-ended question generation or adaptation, and answer parsing; several of these steps were only available in the closest work as an un-released internal pipeline.
experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires building or adapting a text-attributed multi-hop QA set with open-ended answers, plus implementing an intermediate-supervision baseline and running both at scale; no single off-the-shelf benchmark was confirmed by the retrieved evidence.
main_risk: The ported setting may differ from the closest work enough that results are not comparable, and building provenance-preserving extraction is itself error-prone, potentially introducing new noise that confounds the comparison.
required_baselines: Retrieval-based multi-hop baseline (subgraph retrieval / GNN-based retrieval)
